Sa'd teaches his sons the Prophet's refuge after prayer from cowardice, decrepit old age, worldly trials and the grave's punishment; the Prophet also sought refuge from helplessness and laziness.
The Prophet sought refuge for Al-Hasan and Al-Husain with Abraham's words for Ishmael and Isaac: Allah's perfect words against every devil, poisonous pest and evil eye.
At the verses on torment from above and below the Prophet sought refuge with Allah's Face, but called party strife and mutual violence lighter.
The Prophet sought refuge with Allah from miserliness, laziness, old age, the punishment of the grave, the Dajjal's affliction and the afflictions of life and death.
On going to the lavatory the Prophet sought refuge with Allah from al-khubuth and al-khaba'ith.

The Prophet sought refuge from worry, grief, incapacity, laziness, miserliness, cowardice, debt, old age, worldly affliction and the grave's punishment, which he confirmed after Aisha doubted two Jewish women.
The Prophet sought refuge from cowardice, miserliness, old age, the trial and punishment of grave and Fire, poverty, wealth and the Dajjal, asking that his sins be washed away.
As verse 6:65 came down, the Prophet sought refuge with Allah's Face from punishment from above and below, and called party strife and mutual violence the easier warnings.
When the verse on torment from above and below came down, the Prophet sought refuge with Allah's Face, and called being split into parties easier.
